The Food Inspector Divi, vs Gunda Pandurangaiah on 11 March,
2024
 1
 The Honourable Sri Justice E.V.Venugopal
 Criminal Appeal No.83 Of 2013
J U D G M E N T:

entities.text: Food Inspector Divi, vs Gunda Pandurangaiah
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The present Criminal Appeal is filed under Sections 378 (1) and (3) of Cr.P.C seeking to set aside the Judgment dated 30.06.2005 passed in C.C.No.416 of 2001 on the file of the learned Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Miryalaguda (for short 'the trial Court').
2.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Miryalaguda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard and perused the record.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 16.04.2001 at about 03.00 PM, Sri K.Atchaiah, Gazetted Food Inspector (Division-I), Nalgonda District (Pw.1) has inspected the business premises of M/s Ramakrishna Flour and Groundnut Oil Mills situated Door No.13-73/1, Seetharampuram,
Miryalguda, where the accused No.1 was present by transacting the business.
On enquiry, the accused No.1 disclosed that he himself is the Managing Partner of the said Oil Mill.
Pw.1 introduced himself to accused No.1 as Food Inspector, Nalgonda District and inspected the said Flour and Groundnut Oil Mill after securing the panchas Pws.2 and 3.
Pw.1 enquired about the nature and purpose of oil stored in loose three tanks.
The accused No.1 disclosed that it is groundnut oil manufactured in the same mill and kept for sale for human consumption.
On suspicion of adulteration, Pw.1 purchased 375 gms of Groundnut Oil for Rs.14-25 paise paid its cost and obtained cash receipt.
Then, Pw.1 served notice in Form No.VI to the accused No.1 and informed that the purchased sample of Groundnut oil would be sent to the public analyst for analysis.

The, Pw.1 divided the purchased groundnut oil into three equal parts, each part was kept into three cleaned, dried, empty bottles and mouth of each bottle was fitted with caps tightly,
tied with thread and sealed, label bearing code No.Sl.No.NLG/DI/11422/2001 were pasted on each sample bottle.
Again each sample bottle was separately wrapped fairly with thick brown paper and the ends were neatly folded in and affixed with gum.

The paper slips bearing Code No. and Sl.No. of the local (Health) Authority was pasted on each sample bottle completely running from bottom to top and around the bottle and obtained the signature of accused No.1 on each sample bottle in such a manner that the paper slip and the wrapped paper both carry a part of the signature.

Further, each sample bottle was tied with thread on all the four sides and affixed four seals with sealing wax using specimen impression seals of Pw.1 on all the four sides i.e., bottom, top and either side of middle of the bottles and covering the knots also.
A panchanama was drafted by Pw.1 and it was attested by The Food Inspector Divi, vs Gunda Pandurangaiah on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198400581/

entities.text: Food Inspector Divi, vs Gunda Pandurangaiah
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1 accused No.1, Pws.1 to 3.
4.

On 17.04.2001 one part of the sample bottle along with Memorandum in Form No.VII was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis in a sealed packet by express parcel service vide postal receipt No.04824 dated 17.04.2001 under intimation to the Local(Health) Authority.
One more copy of Form No.VII Memorandum with specimen impression seal of Pw.1 was sent to Public Analyst by Registered Post vide postal receipt No.04825 dated 17.04.2001.
The remaining two parts of sample along with Form No.VII in duplicate were sent to Local (Health) Authority by express parcel service vide postal receipt Nos.0825 dated 17.04.2001.
After causing analysis, the sample of groundnut oil was declared as adulterated vide report No.323 of 2001, dated 10.05.2001 and the same was sent to the Local (Health) Authority on 11.05.2001.
Thereafter, the report was forwarded to the Pw.1 for necessary action.

In the report of the Public Analyst opined that the sample does not conform to the standards of Bellier's Tes (Turbidity Temperature Acetic Acid Method) and red units in respect Halphen's Test for cotton seed oil, contains cotton seed oil and therefore, it is adulterated.
Pw.1 received sanction order from the State Food (Health) Authority.
Hence, the complaint.

5. In order to prove its case, the prosecution got examined Pws.1 to 3 and got marked Exs.P-1 to P-24.
6.

After appreciating the oral and documentary evidence on record, the trial Court has observed that prosecution has failed to establish the guilt of the respondents/accused Nos.1 and 2 for the offences punishable under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for a contravention of Section 7(i)(v) and 2(ia)(m) of P.F.A Act, 1954.

Hence, they are found not guilty of the said offences and are acquitted under Section 248 (1) Cr.P.C.
7.
Aggrieved by the judgment passed by the trial Court, the appellant/State has preferred the present criminal appeal.

8. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for appellant-State would submit that:
(i) the trial Court ought to have seen that Pw.1 followed all the mandatory provisions as laid down under the PFA Act and the sole testimony of Pw.1 is sufficient to base conviction.
(ii) the learned judge ought to have seen that it is not necessary for Public Analyst to mention the proceedings of adulteration mere presence of cotton seed oil amounts to adulteration.
(iii) the trial Court failed to appreciate the facts and evidence available on record and erroneously acquitted the accused on flimsy and untenable grounds.
That cannot be a ground doubting the prosecution case and the Court cannot give acquittal to the respondents/accused persons.
Hence seeks to allow the present criminal appeal.

2 9.

sentences.text: Recording the submissions made by the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor and upon perusing the entire material available on record, there are no grounds to interfere with the well reasoned order dated 30.06.2005 passed by the trial Court in C.C.No.416 of 2001.
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to entertain the present Criminal Appeal.
10. With the above observations, the present Criminal Appeal is dismissed.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.

___ JUSTICE E.V.VENUGOPAL Dated: 11.03.2024 mmr The Food Inspector Divi, vs Gunda Pandurangaiah on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198400581/
